title: Statistics - Comparing Data Sets Using Central Tendency and Spread
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: Class A has a mean score of 72 and Class B has a mean score of 68. Both classes have the same standard deviation. Which class performed better on average?
questions.explanation: The mean measures average performance. Since Class A has a higher mean (72 > 68) and both have the same spread, Class A performed better on average.

questions.question: Two data sets have the same median of 50. Data Set X has IQR = 12 and Data Set Y has IQR = 28. Which data set has more consistent values in the middle 50%?
questions.explanation: A smaller IQR indicates the middle 50% of values are more tightly clustered. Data Set X (IQR=12) has more consistent middle values than Data Set Y (IQR=28).

questions.question: Given Σx = 200, Σx² = 4200, and n = 10 for Data Set P. What is the standard deviation?
Data Set M has mean = 45, SD = 8. Data Set N has mean = 45, SD = 3. Which statement is correct?
options: Data Set M has more consistent values
Data Set N has more consistent values
questions.explanation: Both sets have the same mean, but Data Set N has a smaller SD (3 < 8), meaning its values are closer to the mean — more consistent.

questions.question: Two classes took the same test. Class P: median = 65, IQR = 10. Class Q: median = 65, IQR = 22. Which class had more students scoring close to the median?
questions.explanation: Same median means same middle value, but Class P has a smaller IQR (10 < 22), meaning more students scored close to the median.

questions.question: Given Σ(x - x̄)² = 96 and n = 24 for a data set. What is the standard deviation?
Data Set A: mean = 30, SD = 5. Data Set B: mean = 30, SD = 15. If a value of 40 appears in both sets, in which set is this value more unusual?
questions.explanation: In Data Set A, 40 is 2 SDs above mean (30+2×5=40). In Data Set B, 40 is less than 1 SD above mean (30+15=45). Values farther from the mean relative to SD are more unusual.

questions.question: Two data sets have identical IQRs. Data Set X has range = 40, Data Set Y has range = 60. Which set likely has more extreme values?
questions.explanation: Same IQR means same middle 50% spread, but Data Set Y has a larger range (60 > 40), suggesting more extreme values at the ends.

questions.question: A teacher calculates Σx = 180, Σx² = 3420, n = 12 for a class test. What is the variance?
questions.explanation: Variance is not tested in O Level E-Math 4052. Students calculate standard deviation directly using SD = √[(Σx²/n) - (mean)²], not variance separately.

questions.question: Data Set P: median = 55, Q1 = 48, Q3 = 62. Data Set Q: median = 55, Q1 = 40, Q3 = 70. Which set has a larger interquartile range?
questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1. Set P: 62-48=14. Set Q: 70-40=30. Data Set Q has larger IQR.

questions.question: Two classes have same mean score. Class X: SD = 6, Class Y: SD = 10. A student scored 12 points above the mean. In which class is this score more impressive?
questions.explanation: In Class X, 12 points above mean = 2 SDs (12÷6=2). In Class Y, 12 points = 1.2 SDs (12÷10=1.2). Being farther from mean in SD units is more impressive.

questions.question: Given a data set with n = 16, Σx = 240, and Σ(x - x̄)² = 144. What is the standard deviation?
Data Set A and Data Set B have same median. Data Set A has smaller IQR and smaller range than Data Set B. Which statement must be true?
options: Data Set A is more consistent overall
Data Set B has higher values
Data Set A has higher mean
questions.explanation: Smaller IQR and range both indicate less spread. With same median, Data Set A's values are more tightly clustered — more consistent overall.

questions.question: A data set has mean = 50. If every value is increased by 10, what happens to the standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to all values shifts the mean but does not change the spread. Standard deviation remains unchanged.

questions.question: Two data sets have same standard deviation. Data Set X has mean = 40, Data Set Y has mean = 60. A value of 50 appears in both sets. In which set is 50 closer to the mean in standard deviation units?
questions.explanation: Distance from mean: |50-40| = 10 for Set X, |50-60| = 10 for Set Y. Since SD is same for both sets, the distance in SD units is identical (10/SD). Therefore, 50 is equally close to the mean in both sets.
